title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 36 (Agreements contingent on impossible events void)

content.overview: Section 36 provides that contingent agreements to do or not to do anything, if an impossible event happens, are void, whether the impossibility of the event is known or not to the parties to the agreement at the time when it is made.
content.glance: Contingent on an impossible event → void, whether impossibility known or not at the time of agreement.
content.study: Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything if an impossible event happens are void, whether or not the parties knew of the impossibility when the agreement was made. Current-law framing: identify the contingency; test impossibility of the event; conclude voidness under s. 36 regardless of the parties’ knowledge.

sections.heading: Impossible event
sections.body: Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything if an impossible event happens are void, whether impossibility known or not at the time of the agreement.

provisions.title: Agreements contingent on impossible events void

examples.title: Impossible contingency
examples.body: A agrees to pay B ₹1,000 if two straight lines enclose a space. The agreement is void under s. 36.

hypotheticals.question: Does knowledge of impossibility matter?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 36 voids the agreement whether the impossibility is known or not to the parties at the time when it is made.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-36
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: The agreement is valid if both parties were unaware of the impossibility.
misconceptions.correction: Section 36 voids contingent agreements on impossible events regardless of the parties’ knowledge.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 36 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the contingency. II. Test impossibility of the event. III. Conclude void under s. 36 regardless of knowledge. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Stress voidness independent of knowledge of impossibility.
